description: How an open document reacts to its file changing on disk, and how an external-edit conflict is resolved (Workspace.save, reconcileExternalChange, ConflictResolver). Every scenario opens `doc.md` in an otherwise empty workspace root with content `base`. `edit` (optional) then replaces the buffer text, which makes it dirty. `disk` (optional) then changes the file: a string rewrites it, null deletes it. Content comparison is by byte count and SHA-256 digest, never by modification time. `action` is one of `reconcile` (the watcher reported a change), `save` (autosave or Ctrl+S) or `resolve:<choice>` with choice keepClio, loadExternal or keepBoth; `resolve` scenarios start from a conflict raised by a reconcile. `diskAfterConflict` (optional) rewrites the file once more after the conflict was raised and before the user resolves it. Results: `unchanged`, `reloaded` (clean buffer adopted the outside text), `conflict` (dirty buffer and different outside text: nothing is written, autosave stops), `deleted` (file gone; the buffer keeps its text and is detached), `saved`, `conflictChanged` (the outside text changed again: nothing is written and a refreshed conflict is raised), `resolved`. `expect.diskText` is the content of doc.md afterwards (null when absent), `bufferText` the buffer text, `dirty` whether unsaved edits remain, `conflict` whether a conflict is pending, `backedBy` the file name the buffer is attached to (null when detached), `extraFiles` other documents in the root, `recovery` the byte contents preserved as recovery copies, and `journalReasons` the sorted reasons of crash-journal records left behind. A successful save clears the document's dirtyBuffer checkpoints; externalConflict checkpoints are kept after a resolution (one when the conflict was raised, one more before keepClio or keepBoth writes) and swept at the next launch (startup recovery removes a record whose bytes already match the file, otherwise preserves it as a recovery copy). Sidecar files (names starting `.clio-`) never remain.

scenarios.name: clean buffer adopts an outside edit
dirty buffer and an outside edit is a conflict
same bytes written back is not a change
dirty buffer, file deleted keeps the text
save over an outside edit raises a conflict and writes nothing
save after the file was deleted writes nothing
keep Clio's text over the outside edit
load the outside text and keep Clio's as a recovery copy
keep both saves Clio's text to a sibling and attaches the buffer to it
an outside edit during review refuses the resolution
